zh: 导言
en: Introduction

zh: 起点
en: THE STARTING POINT

zh: 大约二十七年前，当我撰写《理性的反抗》一书时，便开始着手《哲学史》。该书讨论马克思主义哲学与现代科学之间的关系。它获得了很大成功，但篇幅远超我最初的预计。出于篇幅考虑，我不得不遗憾地删去第一部分；这一部分论述哲学史，一直写到马克思那场伟大的革命：辩证唯物主义理论。
en: I first started work on The History of Philosophy some twenty-seven years ago, when writing Reason in Revolt, a book that dealt with the relationship between Marxist philosophy and modern science. The book was a big success, but it turned out to be much longer than I had originally anticipated. Due to considerations of length, I was reluctantly obliged to omit the first part, which dealt with the history of philosophy, leading up to Marx’s great revolution, the theory of dialectical materialism.

zh: 我原本打算在将来某个时候把《哲学史》作为独立著作出版。但由于种种原因，这一决定被推迟，以便腾出时间处理更紧迫的任务。二十多年来，手稿被搁置一旁，任由老鼠的牙齿去批判——正如马克思谈到《德意志意识形态》未发表手稿时所说。它最终在我们的网站上发布，并获得了好评，但把它作为独立书籍出版的初衷，直到现在才实现。
en: The intention had been to publish The History of Philosophy as a separate work sometime in the future. But for different reasons, that decision was delayed to make way for more pressing tasks. For more than two decades, the manuscript was put to one side, left to the gnawing criticism of the mice, as Marx once said, referring to the unpublished text of the German Ideology. It was eventually published on our website, and was favourably received, but the original intention of publishing it as a book remained unfulfilled until now.

zh: 多亏若干对哲学特别感兴趣的同志敦促，我才被激励起来着手出版这部作品。它代表了国际马克思主义趋势在反对资产阶级意识形态、捍卫和传播马克思主义思想这一持续斗争中的一项贡献。这是一个及时而必要的决定。在资本主义制度陷入走向终结的危机的当下，现行秩序的破产必然体现在智识生活各个方面的明显衰退上。
en: I owe it to the pressure of a number of comrades with a special interest in philosophy that I have been spurred into action to publish this work. It represents a contribution to the ongoing campaign of the International Marxist Tendency to combat bourgeois ideology and to defend and propagate the ideas of Marxism. This was a timely and necessary decision. At a time when the capitalist system finds itself in a terminal crisis, the bankruptcy of the existing order inevitably finds its expression in an evident decline of every aspect of intellectual life.

zh: 这一点在哲学领域尤为突出，资产阶级思想正以最令人发指的方式表现其腐朽。争取社会主义的斗争不仅限于政治和经济领域。必须在各个层面展开，首先从思想层面开始。如果本书能帮助工人和青年在这场必要的斗争中武装自己，那么我的目的就达到了。
en: This is particularly glaring in the field of philosophy, where bourgeois thought expresses its decay in a most scandalous manner. The struggle for socialism is not confined to politics and economics. It must be carried on at all levels, starting with the level of ideas. If the present work helps to arm the workers and youth in this necessary struggle, my aim will have been achieved.

zh: 读过原稿的人会发现，所有实质性内容都得以保留。但我已在同志们的协助下彻底修订了文本，并增补了新的小节，尤其是在论述中世纪的那一章中，还增加了最后一章，阐明为什么哲学——至少在该词的旧义上——随着马克思主义而终结。
en: Those who have read the original manuscript will see that, in all essential points, it has been maintained. But I have revised the text thoroughly with the assistance of comrades, and have added new sections, notably in the chapter on the Middle Ages, and also added a final chapter, which explains why philosophy – at least in the old sense of the word – comes to an end with Marxism.

zh: 你们可能还注意到，此前作为附录收录的关于印度哲学的增补章节在本版中被省略，而关于伊斯兰哲学的章节则被缩减，主要论述它在中世纪所扮演的角色。这既非偶然，也非因为我对该主题缺乏兴趣。恰恰相反。你们会理解，呈现两千五百年的哲学是一项非常艰巨的任务，出于篇幅原因，我不得不省略该主题的许多重要方面，只保留最基本的要素。
en: You may also have noticed that the additional chapter on Indian philosophy that was included as an appendix has been omitted from the present edition, while the chapter on Islamic philosophy has been reduced, dealing mainly with the role it played in the Middle ages. This was neither accidental nor due to any lack of interest on my part. Quite the opposite, in fact. As you will appreciate, the presentation of two-and-a-half millennia of philosophy is a very daunting task, and for reasons of space I was compelled to omit many important aspects of the subject, which had to be stripped of all but the most basic essentials.

zh: 东方哲学的发展（其中必须包括中国哲学——这本身就是一个巨大的主题）与西方哲学的发展路线相当不同，西方哲学在黑格尔那里达到顶峰，并在马克思和恩格斯带来的哲学革命中达到顶点。要充分论述那个主题，不仅需要对本书进行巨大（且完全没有必要）的扩充，而且需要另外一卷或多卷著作。因此，与其发表一篇对如此复杂主题的不令人满意的概述——这不会让任何人满意，尤其不会让我自己满意——我决定把这个主题放在一边，打算在时间和工作的压力允许时也许再回到它。
en: The evolution of Oriental philosophy (which would have to encompass Chinese philosophy – a vast topic in itself) proceeded on quite different lines to that of philosophy in the West, which reached its peak in Hegel and culminated in the philosophical revolution brought about by Marx and Engels. To do justice to that subject would have required not merely a huge (and quite unwarranted) expansion of the present book, but would have demanded one or more additional volumes. Therefore, rather than publish an unsatisfactory résumé of quite a complicated subject, which would please nobody, least of all myself, I decided to set this subject to one side, with the intention of perhaps returning to it when the pressure of time and work allows.

zh: 什么是哲学？
en: WHAT IS PHILOSOPHY?

zh: 马克思主义最初是一种哲学，而马克思主义的哲学方法对于理解马克思和恩格斯的思想具有根本性的重要意义。但什么是哲学？
en: Marxism began as a philosophy, and the philosophical method of Marxism is of fundamental importance in understanding the ideas of Marx and Engels. But what is philosophy?

zh: 哲学是一种思维方式，不同于我们日常生活中习惯的那种思维。它并不局限于日常生活中的眼前问题，而是试图探讨生死、宇宙、思想与物质的本质，以及何为善、何为恶等重大问题。这些问题对我们每个人来说，归根结底都至关重要。然而，它们通常并不占据大多数人思想中的核心位置。
en: Philosophy is a way of thinking, different from the kind of thinking we are used to in ordinary life. It does not confine itself to the immediate questions of daily life but attempts to grapple with the big questions of life and death, the universe, the nature of ideas and matter, and what is good and what is bad. These are issues that ultimately are of great importance to every one of us. Yet they do not normally occupy a central place in the thoughts of most people.

zh: 纵观整个历史，至少直到今天，大多数人的心思主要都沉浸在日常的生存斗争中。他们完全被诸如“下周我还有工作吗？”“手头的钱够撑到月底吗？”“我还有栖身之所吗？孩子能上学吗？”等等琐碎的问题所占据。
en: For the whole of history, at least up to the present time, the minds of most men and women have been mainly absorbed by the daily struggle for existence. They are fully occupied with such mundane questions as: will I have a job next week? Will I have enough money to last until the end of the month? Will I have a roof over my head, a school for my children, and so on and so forth.

zh: 然而，人类的思想能够成就远为宏大的事业。思想史涵盖了艺术史——始于拉斯科和阿尔塔米拉那些精美的洞穴壁画；科学史——它使我们能够征服自然，将手伸向群星；以及哲学史——其中蕴含着许多惊人的洞见。
en: Yet human thought is capable of far greater things. The history of thought includes the history of art, beginning with the wonderful cave paintings of Lascaux and Altamira; the history of science, which has enabled us to conquer nature and reach out our hands to the stars; and also the history of philosophy, with its many astonishing insights.

zh: 只要人类开始尝试在不借助超自然力量——诸如神灵以及从最原始时代沿袭下来的其他宗教迷信元素——的情况下解释世界，哲学便应运而生。这标志着对自然和我们自身的科学理解的开端。
en: Philosophy emerges as soon as men and women begin to try to explain the world without the intervention of supernatural agencies: gods and goddesses and all the rest of the superstitious paraphernalia of religion that have been carried over from the most primitive times. It marks the beginning of a scientific understanding of nature and of ourselves.

zh: 一种革命性的世界观
en: A REVOLUTIONARY WORLD OUTLOOK

zh: 马克思主义首先是一种世界观，或者如果你愿意，也可以称之为哲学。它的涵盖范围极其广泛。它既是一门历史理论和经济学理论，也是一部革命行动的指南。但马克思的思想从何而来？它们并非凭空而来。马克思本人曾解释说，他的思想主要有三个来源：一是英国古典资产阶级经济学（亚当·斯密和大卫·李嘉图）；二是空想社会主义的勇敢先驱：法国人圣西门和傅立叶，以及我的威尔士同胞罗伯特·欧文。
en: Marxism is first and foremost a world outlook, or philosophy if you prefer. It has a vast scope. It is a theory of history and of economics, and also a guide to revolutionary action. But where did Marx get his ideas from? They did not drop from the clouds. Marx himself explained that there were three main sources to his ideas: there was English classical bourgeois economics (Adam Smith and David Ricardo), then there were the bold pioneers of utopian socialism: the Frenchmen Saint-Simon and Fourier, and my fellow Welshman Robert Owen.

zh: 但在马克思和恩格斯思想形成初期，首要且最重要的因素无疑是德国古典哲学，尤其是黑格尔。而这又是一段漫长时期内多种不同哲学流派发展的产物。现在，要否定空想社会主义者的思想（就像杜林所做的那样）其实很容易。但更恰当的做法，难道不是应该赞扬他们对社会主义历史的非凡贡献，并承认他们的思想在马克思主义形成阶段所发挥的作用吗？
en: But the first and most important element in the formative stages of the ideas of Marx and Engels was without doubt German classical philosophy, particularly Hegel. And this, in turn, was the product of a lengthy period of the development of many different schools of philosophical thought. Now, it would be very easy to dismiss, for example, the ideas of the utopian socialists (as Dühring did). But surely it is more appropriate to pay tribute to their remarkable contribution to the history of socialism and to recognise the part their ideas played in the formative stage of Marxism?

zh: 我最近重读了罗伯特·欧文的部分著作，可以告诉大家，他的一些思想在今天看来依然颇具革命性。这是否意味着，我们在向欧文致敬的同时，就主张回归空想社会主义的思想？当然不是！但无法否认的是，这些思想在科学社会主义的发展过程中发挥了重要作用。这是一个简单的事实。
en: I recently re-read parts of Robert Owen and I can tell you that some of his ideas are still quite revolutionary today. Does that mean that, in paying tribute to Owen, we advocate going back to the ideas of utopian socialism? Of course not! But it is impossible to deny that these ideas played an important role in the development of scientific socialism. This is a simple fact.

zh: 我偶尔会遇到一种相当幼稚的偏见，认为马克思和恩格斯之前的一切都可以被视为保守和反动而予以抛弃。确实，不仅黑格尔，亚当·斯密和李嘉图也是“上层阶级思想家”。有些愚蠢的人以为，仅凭这一事实就足以剥夺他们作为伟大革命思想家的资格。确实，其中一些人（尽管绝非全部）所持的政治观点倾向于保守主义，甚至反动。黑格尔本人在政治观点上就是保守的，尽管他年轻时曾同情法国大革命。但这并不改变这样一个事实：他的辩证方法包含着非常革命性的要素——这一事实甚至被反动的普鲁士当局所承认，他们对黑格尔心存疑虑，甚至怀疑他持有无神论和颠覆性观点。
en: I have occasionally come across a rather childish prejudice that imagines that everything that came before Marx and Engels can be discarded as conservative and reactionary. It is quite true that not only Hegel but also Adam Smith and Ricardo were ‘upper class thinkers’. Some foolish people imagine that this fact alone would be sufficient to disqualify them as great revolutionary thinkers. It is also true that some of them (though by no means all) held political views that tended towards conservatism, or even reaction. Hegel himself was conservative in his political views, although in his younger years he sympathised with the French Revolution. But that does not alter the fact that his dialectical method contained a very revolutionary element – a fact that was recognised by the reactionary Prussian authorities, who regarded Hegel with suspicion, and even suspected him of atheism and subversive views.

zh: 马克思很久以前就指出，每个时代的统治思想就是统治阶级的思想。这些人代表了他们那个时代最先进的思想，而马克思正是以这些思想为基础的。由亚当·斯密发现并由李嘉图发展的价值规律，直接通向马克思的剩余价值理论；而黑格尔的唯心主义辩证法则催生了辩证唯物主义。认为马克思主义者可以无视过去的思想，这种观点与某些极端无政府主义者的偏见同样愚蠢——他们认为，为了建立一个新的无阶级社会，必须摧毁一切过去的事物并从头再造。这是空想主义的精髓所在，若我们接受这一观点，便会彻底排除在实践中进行社会主义革命的可能性。
en: Marx explained long ago that the ruling ideas of every epoch are the ideas of the ruling class. These men represented the most advanced thought of their day and Marx based himself on these ideas. The law of value that was discovered by Adam Smith and developed by Ricardo led directly to Marx’s theory of surplus value, and the idealist dialectic of Hegel led to dialectical materialism. The idea that Marxists can ignore the ideas of the past is as stupid as the prejudice held by some extreme anarchists that, in order to build a new classless society, it is necessary to destroy everything that has gone before and build it anew. This is the distilled essence of utopianism and, if we were to accept it, we would rule out the possibility of carrying out a socialist revolution in practice.

zh: 社会主义革命不会摧毁资本主义现有的成就，相反，它将以此为基础，赋予其截然不同的社会和阶级内涵。科学技术成就将不再服务于微小的寄生统治阶级的利益，而是会根据全社会的利益进行协调规划。我们将利用旧社会留下的“砖块”来建设新社会，原因很简单：没有其他现成的“砖块”可以用于此目的。
en: A socialist revolution would not destroy the existing achievements of capitalism but, on the contrary, would build on them, filling them with an entirely different social and class content. The achievements of science and technology would no longer serve the interests of a tiny parasitic ruling class, but would be planned harmoniously in the interests of the whole of society. We will build the new society, using the bricks left over by the old, for the simple reason that no other ready-made bricks exist for the purpose.

zh: 正如我们要利用从旧社会继承下来的现有生产力——土地、工厂、科学技术——一样，我们也应当以过去发展起来的最先进思想为基础。马克思主义否定了黑格尔的唯心主义，同时保留了其辩证法中一切进步和革命的内容。科学社会主义的奠基者们挽救了辩证法——这种辩证法在黑格尔手中被扭曲为一种唯心主义的形态——并首次将其建立在坚实的唯物主义基础上。通过这样做，他们创造了一种强大的武器，用于按照革命路线改变社会。
en: In the same way that we would make use of the existing productive forces – the land, the factories, science and technology – inherited from the old society, so we should base ourselves on the most advanced ideas developed in the past. Marxism negated Hegel’s idealism, while simultaneously preserving all that was progressive and revolutionary in his dialectical method. The founders of scientific socialism rescued the dialectic, which in the hands of Hegel was presented in a distorted, idealist guise, and placed it for the first time on a sound materialist foundation. In doing so, they created a powerful weapon for changing society along revolutionary lines.

zh: 为什么要学习哲学史？
en: WHY STUDY THE HISTORY OF PHILOSOPHY?

zh: 马克思和恩格斯的全部著作都基于一种明确的哲学方法——辩证唯物主义，若脱离这一方法，便无法理解这些著作。二十世纪马克思主义思想最杰出的代表——列宁和托洛茨基的作品也是如此。古希腊人早已知晓辩证法，后来黑格尔对其进行了发展。辩证唯物主义的基本思想并不难理解。像所有伟大的思想一样，它们本质上是简单的，而且正因其简单而美丽。
en: All the writings of Marx and Engels are based on a definite philosophical method and cannot be understood without it, the method of dialectical materialism. The same is true of the works of Lenin and Trotsky, the most outstanding representatives of Marxist thought in the twentieth century. Dialectics was already known to the ancient Greeks and was later developed by Hegel. The basic ideas of dialectical materialism are not so difficult to grasp. Like all great ideas, they are essentially simple, and they are beautiful in their simplicity.

zh: 然而，太多自认为是马克思主义者的人满足于重复几个基本观点，却从未思考过自己所言的深层含义。这样的“马克思主义者”就像一个死记硬背乘法表的小孩，或者更确切地说，像一只通过模仿人类语言学会重复某些句子、却对其含义一无所知的鹦鹉。要想全面理解辩证唯物主义，必须进行大量细致的研究。目前，我正在撰写一部关于马克思主义哲学的更全面的著作，希望它能帮助阐明其中涉及的更为复杂的问题。
en: But all too many who regard themselves as Marxists are content to repeat a few basic ideas without giving any thought to the deeper meaning of what they are saying. Such ‘Marxists’ resemble a young child who has learned to recite the multiplication tables by rote, or rather, a parrot that has learned by imitating human speech to repeat certain sentences, without having the vaguest understanding of their meaning. In order to arrive at a full understanding of dialectical materialism, a great deal of careful study will be necessary. At the moment, I am working on a further comprehensive work on Marxist philosophy, which I hope will help to clarify the more complicated questions involved.

zh: 但在研究哲学（尤其是马克思主义哲学）时，存在一个难题，而这个难题正是本书的核心所在。当马克思和恩格斯论述辩证唯物主义时，他们可以预设，至少当时受过教育的读者具备哲学史的基本知识。如今，这种预设已不再可能。
en: But there is a difficulty involved in the study of philosophy in general, and Marxist philosophy in particular, and one that lies at the heart of the present work. When Marx and Engels wrote about dialectical materialism, they could presuppose a basic knowledge of the history of philosophy on the part of at least the educated reading public of the day. Nowadays, it is impossible to make such an assumption.

zh: 黑格尔的《哲学史》
en: HEGEL’S ‘HISTORY OF PHILOSOPHY’

zh: 我十七岁还在上学时，便开始阅读黑格尔那部鸿篇巨制——三卷本的《哲学史》。上大学前，我读完了第一卷全书和第二卷的一半。我发现这本书绝对引人入胜。就在我眼前，两千五百年来最深刻的人类思想，以一种极具说服力、清晰而全面的辩证方式展现在我面前。
en: I first began reading Hegel’s monumental, three-volume History of Philosophy when I was seventeen years old and still in school. I got through the whole of the first volume and half of the second before going to university. I found it absolutely riveting. Here, before my very eyes was two-and-a-half-thousand years of the most profound human thought, set forth in a compellingly clear and comprehensive dialectical manner.

zh: 我至今仍保留着几本学生时代的笔记本，里面满是我当时对《哲学史》、《历史哲学》和《精神现象学》所做的笔记。我甚至还有一本笔记本，里面抄录了黑格尔《哲学科学百科全书》中《小逻辑》的大段内容。我曾四处寻找这部杰作却一无所获，但当我最终从一家参考图书馆借到一本时，却发现竟是德文原版！不过，这样的细节并没能让我却步。当时我的德语水平相当不错，于是便开始阅读并做笔记。遗憾的是，那本笔记本在我旅途中遗失了。
en: I still possess several school notebooks full of the notes I made at the time on the History of Philosophy, the Philosophy of History and the Phenomenology of Spirit. I even had a notebook in which I had copied out extensive sections of Hegel’s Shorter Logic from The Encyclopaedia of Philosophical Science. I had searched in vain for a copy of that remarkable work, but when I finally obtained one from a reference library, it turned out to be in the original German! But I was not to be put off by such a detail. At the time, my knowledge of the German language was pretty good, so I set about reading it and taking notes. Unfortunately, that particular notebook got lost in the course of my travels.

zh: 自那以后，我对黑格尔的热情便一直延续至今。关于《哲学史》，最令我印象深刻的是黑格尔处理这一主题时极具原创性的方式。他并未将其呈现为一系列偶然的发展，而是视为一个有机整体——一个通过一系列矛盾而演变的过程，其中一套思想似乎否定了前一套，从而导致人类思想发展形成一个无尽的螺旋。
en: That enthusiasm for Hegel has remained with me ever since. What struck me about the History of Philosophy was the highly original way in which Hegel approached the subject. It is presented not as a series of accidental developments, but as an organic whole – a process that evolved through a series of contradictions, in which one set of ideas apparently negates a previous one, leading to an endless spiral of development of human thought.

zh: 当然，人们或许会对黑格尔处理哲学史的唯心主义方法提出批评。但最重要的是要看到贯穿他所有著作的辩证方法。当其他人只看到一堆互不关联的思想、偶然事件和个别天才时，黑格尔却率先洞察到一个具有自身规律和内在逻辑的有机过程。
en: Of course, one may find fault with Hegel’s idealist approach to the history of philosophy. But the most important thing to see is the dialectical method that characterises all of his works. Where others only saw a mass of unconnected ideas, accidents and individual geniuses, Hegel was the first to see an organic process with a law and an inner logic of its own.

zh: 在哲学通过一系列矛盾发展的过程中，黑格尔不仅将其视为一种否定过程——即一套思想消灭另一套思想的过程。他认识到，这种否定过程同时也意味着对前一阶段中一切有效且真实内容的保留。这种既否定又保留的观念，就是他所说的“扬弃”，并在《精神现象学》的序言中以最崇高的语言表达出来：
en: In the development of philosophy through a series of contradictions, Hegel saw not merely a negative process, whereby one set of ideas annihilated another. He understood that this process of negation also implied the preservation of all that was valid and true in previous stages. This idea of negation that at the same time preserves is what he called sublation, and it is expressed in the most sublime language in his introduction to the Phenomenology of Spirit:

zh: 花蕾在花朵绽放时消失，人们可以说花蕾被花朵否定了；同样，当果实出现时，花朵就被宣告为植物的一种虚假的定在［形式］，而果实则取代花朵，成为植物的真理。这些形式不仅彼此不同，而且作为互不相容的东西相互排斥。然而，与此同时，它们流动的本性使它们成为有机统一体的环节，在其中它们不仅不相互冲突，而且每一个都同样必要；正是这种共同的必要性，构成了整体的生命。
en: The bud disappears when the blossom bursts forth, and one could say that the bud is refuted by the blossom; similarly, when the fruit appears, the blossom is declared to be a false Being-there [form] of the plant, and the fruit replaces the blossom as the truth of the plant. These forms are not only different, they also supplant one another as mutually incompatible. Yet at the same time their fluid nature makes them moments of the organic unity, in which they not only do not conflict, but each is as necessary as the other; and this shared necessity alone constitutes the life of the whole.

zh: 恩格斯在评论黑格尔的《历史哲学》时指出，这种方法代表了一次巨大的进步：
en: Engels, commenting on Hegel’s Philosophy of History, said this method represented a colossal step forward:

zh: 他是第一个试图证明历史中存在发展、存在内在连贯性的人；尽管他的历史哲学中有些内容在今天看来或许有些奇怪，但与他之前或之后敢于对历史提出一般性见解的人相比，其基本构想的宏伟气魄至今仍令人钦佩。
en: He was the first to try to demonstrate that there is development, an intrinsic coherence in history, and however strange some things in his philosophy of history may seem to us now, the grandeur of the basic conception is still admirable today, compared both with his predecessors or those who following him ventured to advance general observations on history.

zh: 尽管存在种种缺陷，黑格尔《哲学史》的宏伟——其恢弘的气魄与深刻的洞见——至今仍令我惊叹不已、钦佩万分。至于那些对黑格尔持后现代批判态度的评论家，我将重申列宁曾论及罗莎·卢森堡时写下的话，其中引用了一则古老的俄罗斯谚语：“雄鹰有时可能飞得比母鸡还低，但母鸡永远无法飞到雄鹰的高度。”
en: For all its faults, the grandeur of Hegel’s History of Philosophy – its majestic sweep and profound insights – is still a source of wonder and admiration to me to this very day. As for the postmodern critics of Hegel, I will repeat what Lenin once wrote about Rosa Luxemburg, quoting the words of an old Russian proverb: “Eagles may at times fly lower than hens, but hens can never rise to the height of eagles.”

zh: 马克思主义的哲学史观
en: THE MARXIST VIEW OF THE HISTORY OF PHILOSOPHY

zh: 在本著作中，我试图利用黑格尔的创新，但始终坚持唯物主义的立场。这并非经验性意义上的哲学史，也不是对历代所有人关于哲学的所有论述的汇编。例如，凡是试图在这部著作中寻找对柏拉图《理想国》的详细研究的人，都会大失所望。对于这样的人，我必须建议他们前往最近的一家正规的公共参考图书馆，我相信在那里他们能找到足够多的博学之作，以满足他们的求知欲。这是一部把握哲学史本质的著作。也就是说，我试图追踪思想发展中的主线，而这条主线有着其自身的内在规律。
en: In the present work, I have attempted to make use of Hegel’s innovation, but from a consistently materialist point of view. This is not a history of philosophy in the empirical notion of the word. Neither is it a compendium of all that everyone ever said on philosophy. Whoever seeks to find in this work, for example, a detailed study of Plato’s Republic, will be sadly disappointed. Such a person I must direct to the nearest serious public reference library, where I trust they may find a sufficient number of erudite works that will satisfy their curiosity. This is a history of philosophy in its essence. That is, I have tried to follow the overarching line in the development of thought, which has its own immanent laws.

zh: 另一方面，我担心本书无法满足那些机械式的“马克思主义者”——他们幻想世间万物皆可归结为生产力和/或阶级斗争的发展。当然，归根结底，这些确实是人类历史的基本驱动力，决定了国度、国家和帝国的命运。但若试图通过强行将其与这一基础建立直接联系，来解释艺术和音乐作品，或是哲学与宗教中那些奇幻的曲折，那将是一种愚蠢的浪费时间。
en: On the other hand, I fear that my book will not satisfy those mechanical ‘Marxists’ who imagine that it is possible to reduce everything under the sun to the development of the productive forces and/or the class struggle. Of course, in the final analysis, these are the fundamental motor forces of human history and determine the fate of countries, states and empires. But to try to find the explanation of, for example, works of art and music, or the fantastic twists and turns of philosophy and religion by imposing a direct link with this substratum would be a foolish waste of time.

zh: 不过，哲学家（如同其他人一样）可能受到社会总体状况——即生产力的兴衰及其引发的社会与政治紧张局势——的影响；就此而言，在某些阶段，这种关系是可辨识的，尽管是间接的，正如我的研究将指出的那样。
en: However, insofar as philosophers (like everybody else) can be affected by the general state of society – the rise and fall of the productive forces and the resulting social and political tensions – a relationship can be discernible at certain stages, albeit an indirect one, as my work will point out.

zh: 正如恩格斯在给德国经济学家康拉德·施密特的信中所写：
en: As Engels wrote in a letter to the German economist Conrad Schmidt:

zh: 至于那些在空中飞得更高的意识形态领域——宗教、哲学等等——它们有一批史前遗留下来的材料，在进入历史时期时就已存在并被继承下来，即我们今天会称之为“胡说八道”的东西。这些关于自然、人类自身、鬼神、魔法力量等等的各种错误观念，在很大程度上只有否定性的经济基础；但史前时期低下的经济发展水平，又被这些错误的自然观念所补充，并且在某种程度上受到其制约，甚至由其所导致。而且，尽管经济必要性是自然知识进步的主要驱动力，并且越来越如此，但如果试图为所有这些原始的无稽之谈寻找经济原因，那无疑是迂腐的。科学史就是逐步清除这些无稽之谈，或者用新的、但已经不那么荒谬的无稽之谈取而代之的历史。
en: As to the realms of ideology which soar still higher in the air, religion, philosophy, etc., these have a prehistoric stock, found already in existence and taken over in the historic period, of what we should to-day call bunk. These various false conceptions of nature, of man’s own being, of spirits, magic forces, etc., have for the most part only a negative economic basis; but the low economic development of the prehistoric period is supplemented and also partially conditioned and even caused by the false conceptions of nature. And even though economic necessity was the main driving force of the progressive knowledge of nature and becomes ever more so, it would surely be pedantic to try and find economic causes for all this primitive nonsense. The history of science is the history of the gradual clearing away of this nonsense or of its replacement by fresh but already less absurd nonsense.
body.review: “否定性的经济基础”对应原文 negative economic basis，紧接着的原文将它与史前经济发展的低下水平联系起来。

zh: 从事这一领域研究的人，在劳动分工中又属于特殊领域，并且在他们自己看来，是在一个独立领域中工作。而且，只要他们在社会分工中形成一个独立群体，他们的产品——包括他们的错误——就会反过来对整个社会的发展，甚至对它的经济发展产生影响。但尽管如此，他们本身仍然受经济发展的主导影响。例如在哲学中，这一点在资产阶级时期最容易得到证明。霍布斯是第一个现代唯物主义者（按十八世纪的意义），但在他那个时代，绝对君主制在整个欧洲正处于顶峰，而在英国，绝对君主制与人民之间的斗争刚刚开始，而他本人是一个君主专制主义者。洛克无论在宗教还是政治上，都是1688 年阶级妥协的产物。英国自然神论者及其更彻底的继承者法国唯物主义者，是资产阶级的真正哲学家，法国唯物主义者甚至是资产阶级革命的哲学家。德国小资产阶级则从康德到黑格尔贯穿德国哲学，有时是正面地，有时是负面地。但是，每个时代的哲学，由于它是劳动分工中的一个确定领域，都以先辈传给它的某些确定的思想材料为前提，并从那里出发。正因如此，经济落后的国家仍然可以在哲学上起主导作用：18 世纪的法国与英国相比——法国哲学正是以英国哲学为基础——以及后来的德国与英法两国相比。但是，法国和德国的哲学，以及当时文学的普遍繁荣，同样也是经济日益发展的结果。我认为，经济发展在这些领域中也具有最终的支配作用，这一点是确定的，但它是在这些领域本身所强加的条件下实现的：例如在哲学中，是通过经济影响（这些影响通常又只是在政治等等的伪装下起作用）作用于先辈传下来的现有哲学材料来实现的。在这里，经济并没有创造任何绝对新的东西（a novo），但它决定了现有思想材料被改变和进一步发展的方式，而且多半是间接地决定的，因为对哲学产生最大直接影响的是政治、法律和道德的反映……这些先生们所缺乏的正是辩证法。他们除了此处的因和彼处的果之外，什么也看不见。他们从未开始看到：这是一种空洞的抽象；这种形而上学的两极对立只在危机时期才存在于现实世界中，而整个广大的发展过程是以相互作用的形式进行的（尽管力量极不平衡，经济运动是最强、最根本、最具决定性的）；在这里，一切都是相对的，没有什么是绝对的。对他们来说，黑格尔从来不存在。
en: The people who deal with this belong in their turn to special spheres in the division of labour and appear to themselves to be working in an independent field. And in so far as they form an independent group within the social division of labour, in so far do their productions, including their errors, react back as an influence upon the whole development of society, even on its economic development. But all the same they themselves remain under the dominating influence of economic development. In philosophy, for instance, this can be most readily proved in the bourgeois period. Hobbes was the first modern materialist (in the eighteenth-century sense) but he was an absolutist in a period when absolute monarchy was at its height throughout the whole of Europe and when the fight of absolute monarchy versus the people was beginning in England. Locke, both in religion and politics, was the child of the class compromise of 1688. The English deists and their more consistent successors, the French materialists, were the true philosophers of the bourgeoisie, the French even of the bourgeois revolution. The German petty bourgeois runs through German philosophy from Kant to Hegel, sometimes positively and sometimes negatively. But the philosophy of every epoch, since it is a definite sphere in the division of labour, has as its presupposition certain definite intellectual material handed down to it by its predecessors, from which it takes its start. And that is why economically backward countries can still play first fiddle in philosophy: France in the eighteenth century compared with England, on whose philosophy the French based themselves, and later Germany in comparison with both. But the philosophy both of France and Germany and the general blossoming of literature at that time were also the result of a rising economic development. I consider the ultimate supremacy of economic development established in these spheres too, but it comes to pass within conditions imposed by the particular sphere itself: in philosophy, for instance, through the operation of economic influences (which again generally only act under political, etc., disguises) upon the existing philosophic material handed down by predecessors. Here economy creates nothing absolutely new (a novo), but it determines the way in which the existing material of thought is altered and further developed, and that too for the most part indirectly, for it is the political, legal and moral reflexes which exercise the greatest direct influence upon philosophy… What these gentlemen all lack is dialectic. They never see anything but here cause and there effect. That this is a hollow abstraction, that such metaphysical polar opposites only exist in the real world during crises, while the whole vast process proceeds in the form of interaction (though of very unequal forces, the economic movement being by far the strongest, most elemental and most decisive) and that here everything is relative and nothing is absolute – this they never begin to see. Hegel has never existed for them.

zh: 我在此试图做的，是勾勒出知识进步过程的本质和总路线；这一过程在历史的每个时代得到充分发展，从而为人类思想迈向下一阶段奠定基础。
en: What I have attempted to do here is to draw out the essential and general course of the process of the advancement of knowledge, the full development of which in each epoch of history lays the ground for human thought to move on to the next stage.

zh: 马克思主义者的任务不是肯定并仅仅剖析曾经存在过的每一个思想学派。相反，它的任务是从无数相互冲突的潮流和观念中，提炼出那些推动人类发展到我们今天这个阶段的本质的、理性的原则。这一过程为科学技术的巨大进步作出了巨大贡献，而这些进步又为人类在社会主义下迈向一个质上更高的发展阶段奠定了基础。
en: The task of Marxists is not to assert and merely dissect every school of thought that ever existed. Rather, it is to draw out from the myriad of conflicting trends and ideas, the essential, rational principles, which have propelled humanity to the stage we are at now. This process has contributed mightily to the enormous advances in science and technology, which in turn lay the basis for humanity’s progression to a qualitatively higher stage of development, under socialism.
body.review: 原文使用 assert and merely dissect，措辞略显生硬；译文保留其肯定／剖析的表述。

zh: 后现代主义对过去的态度：若无知是福，明智便是愚蠢
en: THE POSTMODERN ATTITUDE TO THE PAST: WHERE IGNORANCE IS BLISS, ’TIS FOLLY TO BE WISE

zh: 辩证法有着非常悠久的历史，始于希腊人、前苏格拉底哲学家，尤其是赫拉克利特。它在黑格尔的著作中达到最高表现。但现代资产阶级哲学的主导潮流却蔑视所有过去的哲学。不仅马克思主义，而且过去的一切伟大思想都被轻率地抛弃，被贴上“元叙事”的标签，毫不犹豫地扔进历史的垃圾堆。
en: Dialectics has a very long history, beginning with the Greeks, the pre-Socratic philosophers and particularly Heraclitus. It reaches its highest expression in the works of Hegel. But the dominant trend in modern bourgeois philosophy treats all past philosophy with contempt. Not only Marxism but all the great ideas of the past are frivolously dismissed, labelled as ‘metanarratives’ and consigned without a second thought to the dustbin of history.

zh: 过去，当资产阶级仍然能够发挥进步作用时，它拥有革命性的意识形态。它产生了伟大而原创的思想家：洛克和霍布斯、卢梭和狄德罗，以及法国启蒙运动的其他革命思想家；康德和黑格尔、亚当·斯密和大卫·李嘉图、牛顿和达尔文。但在衰落时期，资产阶级的智识生产显示出晚期衰老的一切证据。
en: In the past, when the bourgeoisie was still capable of playing a progressive role, it had a revolutionary ideology. It produced great and original thinkers: Locke and Hobbes, Rousseau and Diderot, and the other revolutionary thinkers of the French Enlightenment: Kant and Hegel, Adam Smith and David Ricardo, Newton and Darwin. But the intellectual production of the bourgeoisie in the period of decline displays all the evidence of advanced senile decay.

zh: 历史上有些时期以悲观、怀疑和绝望的情绪为特征。在这样的时期，人们已经对现存社会及其意识形态失去信心，只有两种选择。一种是挑战现存秩序，走革命道路。另一种是向内退缩，徒劳地试图无视社会中的矛盾，在宗教或极端哲学主观主义中寻求个人救赎。
en: There are periods in history that are characterised by moods of pessimism, doubt and despair. In such periods, having lost faith in the existing society and its ideology, people have only two alternatives. One is to challenge the existing order and take the revolutionary road. The other is to turn inwards in a futile attempt to ignore the contradictions in society, seeking personal salvation, either in religion or in extreme philosophical subjectivism.

zh: 旧社会正在垂死挣扎，但它顽固地拒绝接受自己的命运。强大的物质利益继续竭力支撑它，它们掌握着可畏的资源，并对社会和智识生活的每一个方面施加不可抗拒的影响。今天，资产阶级的意识形态正在瓦解，不仅在经济和政治领域，而且在哲学领域。它没有产生任何有价值的东西。它不再能赢得积极的支持、尊重或权威，而是散发出消极的情绪，就像尸体散发恶臭。这些情绪不可避免地表现在流行的哲学中。阅读大学哲学系那些贫瘠的产品，不可能不感到同样程度的厌倦和恼怒。不用说，这种普遍倒退也反映在对待哲学史的态度上。
en: The old society is dying on its feet, but it refuses stubbornly to accept its fate. Powerful material interests continue to exert a determined effort to prop it up, and they command formidable resources and exert an irresistible influence on every aspect of social and intellectual life. Today, the ideology of the bourgeoisie is in the process of disintegration, not only in the fields of economics and politics but also in that of philosophy. It produces nothing of value. No longer commanding positive support, respect or authority, it emanates negative moods, as a corpse emits a bad odour. These moods inevitably find their expression in the prevailing philosophy. It is impossible to read the barren products of the university philosophy departments without a feeling of tedium and irritation in equal measure. Needless to say, this general retrogression finds its reflection in attitudes towards the history of philosophy.

zh: 那些怀着启蒙希望、眼神明亮地进入哲学系的年轻学生，要么迅速幻灭，要么被拖入后现代胡言乱语的毒粪坑，从此无法逃脱。无论哪种情况，他们出来时都没有从过去的伟大思想家那里学到任何有价值的东西。哲学系不满足于用后现代主义垃圾填满年轻人的头脑，还胆敢把同样的垃圾引入对过去的研究。显然，后现代学术帮派不喜欢被提醒这样一个事实：曾经有一个时代，哲学家们实际上对现实世界说过一些深刻而重要的话。
en: The bright-eyed young students who enter the philosophy departments with high hopes of enlightenment are either swiftly disenchanted or else dragged into the poisonous cesspool of postmodern gibberish from whence no escape is possible. In either case, they will emerge without ever learning anything of value from the great thinkers of the past. Not content with filling the minds of young people with postmodernist rubbish, the philosophy departments have the audacity to introduce the same garbage into the study of the past. Evidently, the postmodern academic gang do not like to be reminded of the fact that there was once a time when philosophers actually had something profound and important to say about the real world.

zh: 哲学史的扭曲
en: THE DISTORTION OF PHILOSOPHICAL HISTORY

zh: 最近有人向我指出，一本新出的（且备受赞誉的）黑格尔译本包含一个严重的德文误译，竟把后现代主义术语放进这位伟大辩证法思想家的口中。剑桥大学出版社新出的、正被全世界大学奉为经典的《逻辑学》英文译本，始终把德文词Denken 和Denkend（英文直译就是“思想”和“思考”）译成“话语”和“话语的”。
en: It was recently pointed out to me that a new (and highly praised) translation of Hegel contains a gross mistranslation from the German, which places the postmodernist terminology in the mouth of that great dialectical thinker. The prestigious new Cambridge University English translation of Hegel’s Science of Logic, which is becoming canonised in universities across the world, consistently translates the German words Denken and Denkend (which in English plainly mean “thought” and “thinking”) as “discourse” and “discursive”.
body.review: 本段对译本的批评及对德文词的解释均为原作者的论断，按原书保留。

zh: 这是对黑格尔思想的公然伪造，是对一切翻译伦理规范的违背。这是一种犯罪式的行为，试图把后现代主义主观主义偷偷塞进黑格尔。译者乔治·迪·乔瓦尼在为这一选择辩护时，毫无证据地随口断言：“《逻辑学》的主题不是‘物自体’或其现象表现，无论人们把它的‘自在’理解为实体还是自由，而是话语本身。”
en: This is a blatant falsification of Hegel’s ideas and a transgression of all the ethical norms of translation. It is a criminal act of trying to sneak postmodernist subjectivism into Hegel. In defending this choice, the translator George di Giovanni casually asserts without any proof that: “The subject matter of the Logic is not the ‘thing-in-itself’ or its phenomenal manifestations, whether one conceives its ‘in-itself’ as a substance or as freedom, but is discourse itself.”

zh: 这简直是一桩丑闻。然而，那些“批评家”却对此视而不见，他们都为这种新“叙事”而欣喜。这是一种破坏行为，大致相当于在蒙娜丽莎的脸上画一撮小胡子。仅这个小细节就应让我们警惕。
en: This is nothing short of a scandal. Yet it has passed unnoticed by the ‘critics’, who are all delighted by the new ‘narrative’. It is an act of vandalism, more or less the equivalent of painting a moustache on the face of the Mona Lisa. This little detail should already put us on our guard.

zh: 虚假的客观性
en: A FALSE OBJECTIVITY

zh: 我毫不怀疑，大学里那些自作聪明的人会立刻指责我呈现了哲学史的片面版本。对于这一指控，我认罪。作为一个坚定的马克思主义者，我完全打算捍卫一个特定的哲学立场——辩证唯物主义的立场。
en: I have not the slightest doubt that the cleverdicks of the universities will lose no time in accusing me of presenting a one-sided version of the history of philosophy. To this accusation, I plead guilty. As a committed Marxist, I have every intention of defending a particular philosophical standpoint – that of dialectical materialism.

zh: 大学哲学系不是知识和文化的象牙塔，而只是阶级战争中的战壕。这些战壕被精心构筑的伪科学虚假客观性伪装巧妙地掩盖起来。但在这张错综复杂的谎言网背后，人们总能发现物质利益、阶级偏见和对现状的犬儒式辩护。
en: The university philosophy departments are not ivory towers of knowledge and culture, but merely trenches in the war between the classes. These trenches are carefully disguised with an artfully constructed camouflage of pseudo-scientific false objectivity. But behind this tangled web of lies one always finds material interests, class prejudice, and a cynical defence of the status quo.

zh: 整个哲学史一直是两种敌对而互不相容的观点之间不断斗争的历史：哲学唯物主义和哲学唯心主义。也就是说，科学态度与试图把人类意识拖回宗教神秘主义世界的企图之间的斗争。既然哲学领域一直被划分为一系列“片面的版本”，那么完全不可能避免站在这种或那种世界观一边。本书作者与批评者之间的唯一区别是：我足够诚实，从一开始就表明了自己的立场，而我的批评者则总是躲在虚伪且完全虚假的“客观性”背后，这种客观性只是用来掩盖他们的有倾向性的观点和阶级立场。
en: The whole history of philosophy has been a constant struggle between two hostile and mutually exclusive viewpoints: philosophical materialism and philosophical idealism. That is to say, the scientific approach and the attempt to drag human consciousness backwards to the world of religious mysticism. Since the field of philosophy has always been divided into a whole series of ‘one-sided versions’, it is utterly impossible to avoid taking the side of one or other of these world views. The only difference between the present author and his critics is that I have been honest enough to declare my interest from the very outset, whereas my critics always hide behind a hypocritical and entirely spurious ‘objectivity’, which merely serves to disguise their partisan views and class standpoint.

zh: 时至今日，哲学仍然是唯物主义和唯心主义之间一场不择手段的战斗，唯物主义的敌人众多且拥有许多优势。但是，采取明确的哲学和政治立场这一事实，是否就排除了客观性呢？
en: To this day, philosophy remains a battle with no holds barred between materialism and idealism, where the enemies of materialism are numerous and have many advantages. But does the fact that one takes up a definite philosophical and political standpoint rule out objectivity?

zh: 这是一个与事实相矛盾的假设。伟大的马克思主义者列昂·托洛茨基曾这样回答这些反对意见：
en: That is an assumption which is contradicted by the facts. That great Marxist Leon Trotsky answered these objections as follows:

zh: 在庸人眼中，革命观点几乎等同于缺乏科学客观性。我们的想法恰恰相反：只有革命者——当然，前提是他掌握了科学方法——才能揭示革命的客观动力。认识性思维一般说来不是静观的，而是能动的。意志要素对于穿透自然和社会的秘密是不可或缺的。正如外科医生的手术刀关乎人的生命，他会极其谨慎地区分有机体的各种组织，革命者如果严肃对待自己的任务，也必须以严谨负责的态度分析社会的结构、功能和反射。
en: In the eyes of a philistine a revolutionary point of view is virtually equivalent to an absence of scientific objectivity. We think just the opposite: only a revolutionist – provided, of course, that he is equipped with the scientific method – is capable of laying bare the objective dynamics of the revolution. Apprehending thought in general is not contemplative, but active. The element of will is indispensable for penetrating the secrets of nature and society. Just as a surgeon, on whose scalpel a human life depends, distinguishes with extreme care between the various tissues of an organism, so a revolutionist, if he has a serious attitude toward his task, is obliged with strict conscientiousness to analyse the structure of society, its functions and reflexes.

zh: 关于我的批评者
en: A WORD ON MY CRITICS

zh: 自从马克思主义作为挑战现存秩序的重要力量出现以来，当权派就一直对马克思主义意识形态的每个方面——首先是辩证唯物主义——处于持续战争状态。只要提到马克思主义，就必然会在这些圈子里引起条件反射式的反应。“过时”、“不科学”、“早已被驳倒”、“形而上学”，以及所有其他陈腐而令人厌倦的反动老调。
en: Ever since Marxism emerged as a significant force challenging the existing order, the establishment has been in a perpetual state of war against every aspect of Marxist ideology, starting with dialectical materialism. The very mention of Marxism is guaranteed to provoke a knee-jerk reaction in such circles. ‘Out of date’, ‘unscientific’, ‘disproved long ago’, ‘metaphysics’, and all the rest of the threadbare and tiresome litany of reaction.

zh: 我毫不怀疑，本书也会受到同样的一片反对声。这丝毫不困扰我。过去六十年里，我一直听着同样冗长乏味的谩骂洪流，而马克思的批评者们的论点，并不会因为被如此频繁而单调地重复而变得更有力。我明白我的对手会因此不快。他们会翻查旧文本，试图证明黑就是白、白就是黑，以此反驳我的论点。这是很自然的反应，因为他们自己捍卫着一种与我的立场完全不相容的特定哲学立场。我指的是哲学唯心主义立场——无论是客观唯心主义还是主观唯心主义。
en: I have no doubt that the present work will be greeted by a similar chorus of disapproval. This does not bother me in the slightest. I have listened to the same tedious torrent of abuse for the last six decades, and the arguments of the critics of Marx do not gain any greater strength from being so frequently and monotonously repeated. I understand that my opponents will be offended by this. They will try to disprove my arguments by burrowing through old texts to try to prove that, after all, black is white and white is black. This is quite a natural reaction, since they themselves defend a particular philosophical standpoint, which is totally incompatible with my own. By that I mean the standpoint of philosophical idealism – either the objective or the subjective kind.

zh: 我当然对此没有异议。他们完全有权捍卫任何吸引他们的神秘和非理性观念。但让他们不要试图用虚假客观性的外衣掩盖自己的偏袒，也不要试图歪曲过去伟大思想家的思想，以迎合他们自己狭隘而反动的观点。
en: I naturally have no objection to this. They have every right to defend whatever mystical and irrational ideas appeal to them. But let them not try to conceal their partiality behind a façade of false objectivity, or attempt to distort the ideas of great thinkers of the past to fit in with their own narrow and reactionary outlook.

zh: 哲学作为革命武器
en: PHILOSOPHY AS A REVOLUTIONARY WEAPON

zh: 尽管官方哲学摆出一副高高在上、蔑视阶级斗争的神气，但它只是统治阶级手中的又一件武器，被蓄意用来迷惑和误导青年，使他们偏离革命道路。用老约瑟夫·狄慈根的话说，哲学不是科学，而是防范社会主义的屏障。
en: In spite of its aura of lofty superiority and contempt for the class struggle, official philosophy is only one more weapon in the hands of the ruling class, and it is used deliberately in order to confuse and disorient the youth, and divert them from the path of revolution. In the words of old Joseph Dietzgen, philosophy is not a science, but the safeguard against socialism.

zh: 从前，哲学家是反叛者，是危险异端，一心要颠覆现存的道德和社会秩序。苏格拉底被迫饮下毒堇汁；斯宾诺莎被指控为无神论，被逐出教门并遭到辱骂；乔尔达诺·布鲁诺被宗教裁判所烧死在火刑柱上；18 世纪法国哲学家们为攻占巴士底狱铺平了道路。然而在我们自己的时代，大多数人对哲学和哲学家要么漠不关心，要么蔑视，而这完全是咎由自取。但最令人深感遗憾的是，人们在避开当今哲学荒漠时，却忽视了过去的伟大思想家——与现代的侏儒相比，他们是人类思想的巨人。
en: In former times, philosophers were rebels, dangerous heretics bent on subverting the existing moral and social order. Socrates was forced to drink hemlock; Spinoza was accused of atheism, excommunicated and reviled; Giordano Bruno was burnt at the stake by the Inquisition; the French philosophes of the eighteenth century prepared the way for the storming of the Bastille. In our own times, however, most people regard philosophy and philosophers with either indifference or contempt, which is richly deserved. But it is a matter of the deepest regret that in turning aside from the present-day philosophical desert, people neglect the great thinkers of the past who, in contrast to the modern pygmies, were giants of human thought.

zh: 旧的唯心主义哲学顽固地维持着一种想象中的、独立于社会生活的地位。直到今天，学术界的哲学家们仍声称自己超脱于真实人类、社会生活与政治的肮脏世界。但这是一种幻觉。实际上，他们只是那个世界的反映，尽管是以神秘化的形式。归根结底，无论他们是否意识到，他们所捍卫的观念都是对现存社会略加掩饰的辩护，而其基础则是最卑劣、最犬儒的个人利益。
en: The old idealist philosophy stubbornly maintained its imaginary independence from social life. To this day, the philosophers of academia claim detachment from the grubby world of real human beings, social life and politics. But this is an illusion. In reality, they merely represent a reflection of that same world, albeit in a mystified form. In the last analysis, whether they are conscious of it or not, the ideas they defend are a thinly disguised defence of the existing society and, at bottom, the most sordid and cynical personal interest.

zh: 就我而言，我无意与那些只受对马克思主义的盲目仇恨和维持现状的热切愿望所驱使的学者跳一场复杂的小步舞。只有清除这些意识形态垃圾，我们才能为成功进行阶级斗争扫清场地。马克思主义有责任为陈旧而信誉扫地的观念提供一个全面的替代方案。但我们无权背弃过去的伟大思想家：希腊人、斯宾诺莎、启蒙运动时期的法国唯物主义者，尤其是黑格尔。这些人是英勇的先驱，为马克思主义哲学的辉煌成就铺平了道路，完全可以被视为我们革命遗产的重要组成部分。
en: For my part, I have no intention of dancing a complicated minuet with academics who are guided only by a blind hatred of Marxism and a fervent desire to maintain the status quo. Only by clearing the decks of this ideological garbage can we clear the ground for the successful pursuit of the class struggle. Marxism has a duty to provide a comprehensive alternative to the old and discredited ideas. But we have no right to turn our backs on the great thinkers of the past: the Greeks, Spinoza, the French materialists of the Enlightenment and, above all, Hegel. These were heroic pioneers, who prepared the way for the brilliant achievements of Marxist philosophy, and can rightly be considered as an important part of our revolutionary heritage.

zh: 我们有责任从哲学史中拯救一切有价值的东西，同时摒弃一切虚假、过时和无用的东西。正如十月革命、巴黎公社和攻占巴士底狱为将改变整个世界的未来社会主义革命指明了道路，过去那些伟大的哲学战斗也为辩证唯物主义——未来的哲学——奠定了基础。正如我们认真关注过去阶级斗争提供的教训，我们也有责任研究构成哲学史本质意义的那场伟大观念战斗。
en: We have a duty to rescue all that was valuable in the history of philosophy, while discarding all that was false, outmoded and useless. Just as the October Revolution, the Paris Commune and the storming of the Bastille pointed the way to the future socialist revolution that will transform the entire world, so the great philosophical battles of the past laid the basis for dialectical materialism – the philosophy of the future. And just as we pay careful attention to the lessons afforded by the class struggles of the past, so we have a duty to study the great battle of ideas that constitutes the essential meaning of the history of philosophy.

zh: 本杰明·法林顿教授：个人回忆录
en: PROFESSOR BENJAMIN FARRINGTON: A PERSONAL MEMOIR

zh: 在本书前几章中，你会注意到我引用了一本名为《希腊科学》的书，这是本杰明·法林顿教授所写的一部享有盛誉、实至名归的研究著作。这是一部开创性著作，在论述这一主题方面从未被超越。如今它一般被视为经典，但它曾引起相当大的争议，因为它是从马克思主义历史唯物主义的立场写成的。我有幸在1963 年见到法林顿教授，那一年我离开斯旺西，进入刚刚开办的苏塞克斯大学。这次会面的原因如下。
en: In the early chapters of this work, you will notice that I quote from a book called Greek Science, a justly celebrated study written by Professor Benjamin Farrington. This was a pioneering work that has never been surpassed in its treatment of this subject. Nowadays it is generally seen as a classic, yet it provoked considerable controversy because it is written from the standpoint of Marxist historical materialism. I had the good fortune to meet with Professor Farrington in 1963, the year when I left Swansea to enter Sussex University, which had only recently opened. The reason for this meeting was as follows.

zh: 法林顿教授出生于爱尔兰，但曾到许多国家教授古典学（希腊语和拉丁语），这是他的主要专长，尽管他也写了关于哲学的重要著作，例如他对英国唯物主义者弗朗西斯·培根的研究。他在南非任教，并很快因其激进观点而闻名。后来他移居英格兰，在布里斯托大学任教，最后定居在我的家乡斯旺西，从1936 年到1956年担任古典学教授，直到退休。三十年代是南威尔士严重萧条、大规模失业和贫困的时期。这也影响了我的家庭，我的祖父——一个马口铁工人——常常很难养活自己的孩子。他是一位活跃的工会活动家，也是共产党的一名坚定成员。
en: Professor Farrington was born in Ireland, but travelled to many countries to teach classics (Greek and Latin) which were his main specialities, although he also wrote important works on philosophy, such as his study of the English materialist, Francis Bacon. He taught in South Africa, where he soon became known for his radical views. Later, he moved to England, where he taught at Bristol University, until he finally settled in my hometown Swansea, where he was Professor of Classics from 1936 to 1956, when he retired. The thirties was a period of severe depression, mass unemployment and poverty in South Wales. That affected my own family, where my grandfather – a tin plate worker – often had a hard time just feeding his children. He was an active trade unionist and a committed member of the Communist Party.

zh: 虽然许多人知道本杰明·法林顿是马克思主义者，但很少有人知道他也是一名共产党员。由于他的职位，这一事实没有公开，这是当时共产党的规矩。他认识了我的祖父和我的母亲，我母亲年轻时曾在斯旺西卖《每日工人报》。他很快成为我们家的挚友。
en: Although many people know that Benjamin Farrington was a Marxist, very few know that he also was a member of the Communist Party. Because of his position, this fact was not made public, as was the rule in the CP in those days. He got to know both my grandfather and my mother, who as a young girl used to sell The Daily Worker in Swansea. He soon became a firm friend of the family.

zh: 当我准备去苏塞克斯时，我母亲没有对我说一个字，就给他写了一封信，骄傲地宣布我要上大学了（这在我们家是闻所未闻的事），并附上了我寄给《南威尔士晚邮报》的两封信，支持古巴革命。鉴于法林顿教授已经退休，而且据我所知已和我家失去一切联系，我惊讶地得知他不仅回了信，还邀请我在去布莱顿的路上到他那里喝茶。他当时已退休，和妻子住在利明顿温泉，我便去那里见他。他非常热情地迎接我，并询问我母亲的情况（我祖父最近去世了）。我记得他是一个非常迷人、友好的人，丝毫没有许多自命不凡的学者那种高高在上的优越感。他说话带着那种柔和、温和的南爱尔兰口音，对我们这些生活在这几个小岛上的非爱尔兰人来说，那简直是音乐。他问起我在苏塞克斯大学的学业，并对我寄给《晚邮报》的信给予非常慷慨的赞扬。他注意到我被四周装满书的书架吸引。看到我对哲学感兴趣，他问我最喜欢的哲学家是谁。我毫不犹豫地回答：黑格尔。他立刻站起来，伸手取下一本灰色旧书，递给我。那是黑格尔的《法哲学原理》。我打开书，开始翻阅，他制止了我。“它是你的了，”他说。“你可以留着。”
en: When I was preparing to go to Sussex, without saying a word to me, my mother sent him a letter in which she proudly announced that I was going to university (an unheard-of event in our family) and enclosed a couple of letters that I had sent to the South Wales Evening Post, in support of the Cuban Revolution. In view of the fact that Professor Farrington had retired and as far as I know had lost all contact with my family, I was astonished to learn that he had not only replied, but had invited me to join him for tea on my way to Brighton. He was now retired and living with his wife in Leamington Spa, where I went to meet him. He greeted me very warmly and enquired after my mother (my grandfather had recently passed away). I remember him as a very charming, friendly man, with no hint of the kind of lofty superiority that is the hallmark of so many pretentious academics. He spoke with that soft, gentle southern Irish accent that is music to the ear of us non-Irish inhabitants of these small islands. He asked me about my studies at Sussex and was very generous in his praise of the letters I had sent to The Evening Post. He noticed that I was fascinated by the shelves that were full of books on all sides. Seeing that I was interested in philosophy, he asked me who my favourite philosopher was. I replied without any hesitation: Hegel. He immediately stood up and reached for an old grey volume, which he handed to me. It was Hegel’s Philosophy of Law. I opened it and started to glance through the pages, when he stopped me. “It’s yours”, he said. “You can keep it.”

zh: 我确实一直保存着那本书，写这些文字时它就放在我的书桌上。这是我的书中唯一一本没有用无数下划线标出、没有在页边写满评论的书。它仍然是一个珍贵纪念，纪念与一位伟人的短暂相遇——一个在现实生活中实属罕见的人：一位学者，不仅是一个真正的知识分子，而且是一个坚定的马克思主义者，不怕独自对抗庸俗之徒。
en: I have indeed kept that volume ever since and it is sitting on my desk as I write these lines. It is the only one of my books that I have not marked with numerous underlinings and comments in the margins. It remains a precious reminder of a brief encounter with a great man – a real exception in this life: an academic who was not only a genuine intellectual but also a committed Marxist who was not afraid to stand alone against the Philistine tribe.

zh: 本杰明·法林顿早已去世，但他的精神激励着本书的每一页。直到今天，对于任何认真研究古希腊历史的人，《希腊科学》都是必读之作。
en: Benjamin Farrington has long since passed away, but his spirit inspired every page of this book. And to this day, for anyone who is seriously interested in the history of ancient Greece, Greek Science is obligatory reading.
London, 20 August 2021
